description: Deterministic, single-threaded discrete-event simulation of the capstone pipeline, shared byte-for-byte between the Java and Rust suites. Each event's decision checksum is a pure function of (key, eventId, eventSizeBytes), never depending on which pipeline variant, shard count, or admission outcome routed it — this is what lets NAIVE and OPTIMIZED assert the identical checksum despite radically different queueing strategies. numShards=1 for NAIVE_OBJECT_QUEUE (a single shared unbounded queue, the anti-pattern baseline); numShards=4 with bounded per-shard admission for every other variant.

mediumEventsHotKeyBurst.note: 80% of events collapse onto key 0 (shard 0) — even though aggregate capacity across 4 shards is generous, shard 0 alone can still overflow under this skew.

variantOverrides.OVERLOAD_PROFILE: Same dataset, but capacityPerShard is forced to capacityPerShard/8 (rounded down, minimum 1) to deliberately induce drops even under a dataset that OPTIMIZED handles cleanly.
variantOverrides.FAULT_RESTART_PROFILE: Same dataset and capacity as OPTIMIZED, but shard 0's queue is forcibly cleared at tick 5 (restartAtTick=5, restartShard=0), and every event still queued there at that moment is counted as restartLoss rather than delivered or dropped.

correctnessInvariant: produced == delivered + dropped + restartLoss, for every (variant, dataset) pair, with zero events left queued at the end of the simulation.
